0.original: The Ishgardian glassworker needs to touch glass.

26.original: Deliver the fetching fragments to the Ishgardian glassworker.

48.original: Ah, an adventurer! A proper adventurer, that is. Out here, we are all adventurers of a sort, are we not?

49.original: In sooth, however, I am a glassworker of Ishgard.

50.original: 'Twas for that expertise that I was invited to take part in the initiative, and I have been quite content to oversee the work at Glassblowers' Beacon.

51.original: Yet as my time here draws to a close, I find myself regretting having failed to venture further afield. I am certain its vistas would inspire me for years to come.

52.original: For that reason, I should like to take a brief stroll─and perhaps collect a few samples that might be incorporated into my future works. Provided you are willing to escort me through the harrowing environs, of course.

53.original: Then I am in your debt. Once you have made your expert preparations for the trials ahead, let us meet to the southwest─within a safe distance of the grotto, of course.

55.original: Oh, forgive me. I was captivated by the scenery.

56.original: I had thought to venture further, but perhaps the inspiration I seek can be gathered right here on our doorstep...

57.original: As an associate of the initiative, you must be a capable artisan in your own right. Why not share in this artistic exercise with me?

58.original: Bring me whatever fetching fragments speak to your aesthetic sense. I shall limit my search to these surrounds, lest I inadvertently endanger myself.

59.original: May we both find some truly fabulous frit!

60.original: You're alive! Did you espy any works of art?

61.original: You have an artisan's eye, indeed. 'Twould be an honor to work with any one of these.

62.original: You may count me thoroughly dazzled by the sights and samples both.

63.original: ...But what of you? You have spent far more time wandering the star than I.

64.original: How have you found your time on Phaenna?

66.original: I've encountered wonders I never could have imagined!

67.original: 'Tis exploration itself I enjoy. For that, Phaenna is beautiful indeed.

70.original: I confess that as beautiful as I find the sea of stars, it frightens me in equal measure.

71.original: How much there is to see...and how limited my own view of it. The moment I stepped outside the grotto, I was nigh overcome.

72.original: I am glad to have glimpsed this star through your eyes, if only for a short while. Come, let us return to the Beacon.

73.original: You have my deepest gratitude, adventurer. I shall never forget the beauty of this <hex:020835E3E90C0DFF17020813E3E90C05FF086576656E696E67FF0464617903FF17020813E3E90C12FF04646179FF086576656E696E670303>.

74.original: And to think that I may have turned down the initiative's invitation were it not for my present struggle at the atelier...

75.original: Not long ago, you see, Lord Aymeric himself commissioned a work of stained glass to celebrate the newfound harmony between man and dragon.

76.original: From the first, I floundered. Long did I know dragons only as terrifying beasts. To see beauty, let alone kinship, in the visage of those creatures? 'Twas beyond even my imagination.

77.original: Now, however, I begin to understand. Even the most fearsome wyrm is but a single soul like you or I, facing the endless expanse with fear...and with wonder.

78.original: I envision a dragon soaring between stars, graceful and strong. Following a glimmer of light across an unimaginable distance...

79.original: A fitting use for this glass, I should think.
